newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo bourse studying reforms of securities market.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo bourse studying reforms of securities market.

text.p: The Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) said on Wednesday it is studying ways of reforming Tokyo's securities market to ensure it thrives in the era of "Big Bang" deregulation of Japan's financial markets.

Among the measures under consideration are new schemes to allow large-lot cross trading of shares and basket-type trading by institutional investors to meet investor demand, an exchange official said.
It is also studying whether it should allow investors to make large-lot stock transactions outside of TSE trading hours, which finish at 3 p.m. (0600 GMT), he said.

The TSE plans to implement the reforms after June, when an advisory panel to the finance minister, the Securities and Exchange Council, unveils a final set of proposals on the timing and details of the Big Bang reforms, he said.

Last week, the advisory panel said in an interim report that Japan should allow transactions of listed stocks to be conducted outside the nation's eight stock exchanges as a spur to competition, while taking steps to ensure that these deals, including electronic transactions, are fairly conducted.
